title: Update Plausible analytics snippet
description:
## Summary

- Replace the old Plausible `<script defer data-domain=...>` tag with the new async snippet that includes `plausible.init()`

## Context

Plausible has updated their recommended tracking snippet. The new format uses `async` loading with an inline init script, and no longer requires the `data-domain` attribute.

title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

title: Fix/precip  to address inconsistent treatment of precipitation
description:
This modifies the precipitation calculation in weather.r to fix an inconsistency. In the raw weather data, precipitation totals are cumulative for the hour and reset to 0 at 51 minutes. Sometimes there is only one weather record for an hour, at 51 minutes, in which case p01i  is the correct hourly total. Other times there are multiple records within an hour, in which case it is necessary to find the maximum reported precipitation earlier than or equal to 51 minutes. (And there are times when there is no 51 minute record.) The existing weather.r takes the first record in the hour, which sometimes gives the hourly cumulative rainfall, but at other times gives whatever rainfall is reported in the first record that hour.

For example consider LGA 2013-06-08 01:00 to 02:00. There are 5 records in the raw data. The first record at 1:16 reports 0.18", which is the precip value reported in the weather data in the package. But the actual hourly cumulative rainfall is for that hour was 0.24" (reported at 01:49 --- this is a case where there is no 51 minute record).

I have been unable to find documentation for the 51 minutes reset time, but it is evident in the data. The code in the pull request generates hourly precipitation that when cumulated matches the official national weather service daily totals (sometimes there is a .01" difference which is made up the next day. I'm not sure why that happens). 

For more details there is [a stackexchange discussion](https://earthscience.stackexchange.com/questions/10598/how-are-daily-precipitation-totals-computed) that I initiated about this issue.

Note that because the raw data download format has changed, the existing weather.r doesn't work, so this fix cannot be tested without also implementing my pull request #24 . I wasn't sure how to handle this so I kept them separate.
